findings.element: Invoices tab → Invoice date lock note 'To change it, change Schedule start date' (RevRec org)
findings.finding: The lock note sends the user to Schedule start date. Picking Invoice issued date there does not move or unlock Invoice date, which stays locked on Created date, so the user cannot reach Issued in books by following the note.
findings.user_impact: A RevRec user who wants issued dates follows the note, picks the matching Invoice issued date option and lands back on a locked Created date. The only way out is to switch Schedule start to Payment date, change Invoice date, then switch Schedule start back, and nothing on screen hints at that.
findings.suggested_fix: When Schedule start is set to an invoice date, make the locked Invoice date follow it (Invoice issued date gives Issued date, Invoice created date gives Created date), or have the lock note say exactly which Schedule start value unlocks it.

evidence.action: Org RevRec · invoice, Invoices tab: read the lock note and click Schedule start date. In RevRec, pick Invoice issued date, click Change, then return to Invoices.
evidence.observed: The state map records the note 'Locked while Revenue Recognition starts schedules from the invoice date. To change it, change Schedule start date.' and says the lock is lifted only when Schedule start = Payment date. In the prototype source, rrLock() is true whenever schedule !== 'payment', and the locked select shows v.syncSaved, so after confirming Invoice issued date the select is still disabled on 'created'.

findings.element: Sync details → Date in books row (present in example A, absent in example B)
findings.finding: The Date in books row only appears when the books date is the issued date. When the invoice was booked on its created date, the screen shows Transaction date and Issued date with nothing saying which one went to the books.
findings.user_impact: A user checking a created-date sync sees two different dates and has to guess which one reached the books, which is the question this screen is supposed to answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the Date in books row in both cases, for example 'Dec 28, 2025 · created date, per Invoice date setting', so the answer is always on screen.

evidence.action: Sync details: switch between example A (synced on issued) and example B (synced on created).
evidence.observed: Example A lists Transaction date Dec 28, Issued date Jan 6 and 'Date in books Jan 6, 2026 · issued date, per Invoice date setting'. In example B the Issued date row stays and the Date in books row disappears.

findings.element: RevRec → Schedule start date confirmation dialog
findings.finding: The dialog lists the effect on schedules but not on the Stripe Invoice date setting, which this choice locks (created or issued) or unlocks (payment).
findings.user_impact: The user confirms without knowing that the Stripe Invoice date setting has just become locked or editable. The cross-screen effect only surfaces later as a disabled control on another screen, which the primary task ('understand what that choice changes') is meant to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to the dialog naming the effect on the Stripe Invoice date setting for the chosen option (locked on its current value or editable again).

evidence.action: RevRec Recognition settings: pick Invoice issued date, read the dialog, click Change. Separately pick Payment date, click Change and open Invoices.
evidence.observed: The dialog reads 'New schedules will start from the invoice issued date. Existing schedules keep their current dates until they’re rebuilt — contact support to rebuild them.' and has no mention of Invoice date. After Payment date, the Invoices select is enabled with no lock note, a change the dialog never mentioned.

gaps: Invoices tab with Schedule start = Invoice issued date is not in the state map. Lock behaviour (stays locked on the saved Created value) was taken from the prototype source (rrLock / screen1), not from a recorded browser interaction.
Learn more, Upgrade plan and How to change links are href='#', so where they go and whether the gate's upgrade path completes is unknown.
No save failure or loading states exist (no backend), so error-state clarity for Update, Summary save-on-change and the RevRec Change could not be assessed.
The dialog body for Invoice created date and Payment date picks was not recorded in the state map, only the Issued text. The wording pattern comes from the source.
